rationale: Start with a broad, mid-temperature scouting gradient to maximize the chance all 10 compounds elute within 42 min and to reveal the overall elution window and critical pairs. The wide phi range and moderate slope should give informative retention spacing without being excessively slow.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only remaining gain is reducing t_last below 10 min. Keep the same wide window and temperature but shorten tG one step to test how much time can be saved before the tightest cluster around peaks 5–7 starts to lose resolution.

We are very close to the 10 min target and the limiting pair still has a little margin at R=1.59, so shorten the gradient one more step at the same conditions. This directly tests whether we can eliminate the remaining time penalty while keeping all pairs at or above 1.5.

The limiting pair lost too much resolution when the gradient was shortened, so try changing temperature rather than slope to recover selectivity while keeping the last peak under 10 min. A 5 C drop may improve the close pair’s ordering/spread with only a modest increase in retention.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity badly, so test the opposite direction at the same fast gradient. A 5 C increase may improve the critical cluster enough to bring the worst pair back toward or above 1.5 while keeping t_last comfortably under 10 min.

The critical pair is highly temperature-sensitive, so return to 40 C and instead narrow the gradient window slightly to make the slope shallower without lengthening the run. Since all peaks likely elute well below 0.90 organic, trimming phi1 should focus gradient time on the actual elution region and may recover the 5–7 cluster.

Narrowing the window helped the critical pair while keeping the last peak under 10 min, so continue one more step in the same direction. The estimated last-peak elution composition is still well below 0.85, so this should further shallow the gradient over the useful range and may lift the 6/7 pair above 1.5.

At phi1 0.85 the critical pair is finally above 1.5, so now shorten tG one step to try to remove the small remaining time penalty. This tests whether the narrower gradient window preserves enough selectivity to keep the worst pair resolved while pulling t_last back under 10 min.

At tG 12 the gradient became too steep for the 6/7 pair, so offset that by slightly widening the window versus injection 8 while keeping the shorter run. This should reduce compression of the critical cluster enough to improve resolution, with a good chance of still keeping t_last under 10 min.

The best current point is close to ideal but still limited by either time or the 6/7 pair, so combine the successful narrower window with a small temperature increase. This probes whether higher T can pull t_last below 10 min without sacrificing the selectivity gain that phi1 0.85 gave to the critical pair.

The first peak is still quite early, so raise phi0 one step while keeping the best-performing phi1, tG, and temperature. This trims unused low-organic range and may shift gradient time toward the crowded middle/late region enough to improve the critical 6/7 pair without pushing t_last above 10 min.

Injection 11 is the best yet, and narrowing phi1 previously improved the critical 6/7 pair at the cost of some retention time. Combining the higher phi0 with phi1 0.85 may further focus the gradient on the actual elution window and lift that pair above 1.5 while hopefully keeping t_last near 10 min.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so the only meaningful next step is to see whether a shorter method can preserve full resolution on the same focused window. Reducing tG by one step tests if the perfect separation can be maintained while making the run faster.

The perfect method has some extra resolution margin on the critical pair, so keep tG 14 and phi1 0.85 but raise phi0 one step to trim early low-organic space and potentially shorten the run while maintaining full resolution. This is a targeted refinement around the optimum rather than changing slope too aggressively.

Raising phi0 to 0.15 preserved a perfect score and shortened the run slightly, so test one more step higher at the same phi1, tG, and temperature. This explores whether further trimming unused low-organic range can keep all pairs above 1.5 while maintaining or improving the fast, fully resolved method.

phi0 0.15 gave a perfect result with some margin, so now test a slightly lower phi1 to further focus the gradient window while staying near the successful conditions. This may retain full resolution and possibly improve the critical 6/7 pair without pushing the last peak past 10 min.

The current optimum at phi0 0.15/phi1 0.85 has solid resolution margin, so test whether a higher temperature can shorten the run while preserving full credit for all pairs. This is a local probe around a proven perfect method to see if time can be reduced without crossing the resolution threshold.

Temperature changes are clearly harmful for the critical pair, so stay at 40 C and make the gradient one step shallower around the best window. This checks whether we can gain a little more robustness on the 6/7 pair while remaining fully resolved, even if it likely will not beat the current perfect methods on speed.

Two perfect methods are already found, so use the remaining budget to map the nearby edge of the optimum by combining the successful higher phi0 with the more selective lower phi1. This tests whether a slightly broader early window than injection 16 can keep all pairs resolved while reducing or eliminating its small time penalty.

The best region is clearly around phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.85, so probe the other side of that optimum by increasing phi1 at phi0 0.15. This defines whether the perfect window is centered near 0.85 or whether a slightly wider upper limit can still keep all pairs resolved while preserving sub-10 min elution.

With the optimum already identified, use one remaining local check to bracket robustness on the shallow side of the perfect phi0 0.10/phi1 0.85 window. A longer tG should comfortably preserve full resolution and helps confirm how much resolution margin exists around that perfect method.

Use the remaining budget to test the fast edge near the other perfect method: phi0 0.15 gave strong performance, and phi1 0.80 gave extra resolution margin, so shortening tG here may reveal a faster fully resolved condition. This is the most plausible unexplored route to another practical optimum near the boundary of full resolution.

Both perfect methods are at 40 C, but the impact of lowering temperature was only tested at a broader window; with the tighter optimum window it is still worth checking whether 35 C can preserve full resolution and perhaps slightly improve selectivity. This maps the temperature edge of the best region without repeating prior conditions.

The lower-temperature test at phi0 0.10 caused a different coelution (5/6), so one final adjacent check at the other perfect window will confirm whether that behavior is general or window-dependent. This cleanly brackets the temperature sensitivity around both optimum compositions.

For the final injection, probe the only remaining nearby fast condition not yet tested around the successful 40 C region: combine the lower phi0 with the more selective phi1 0.80 and shorter tG 12. This checks one last plausible route to a faster fully resolved method, even though the current best CRF is already maximal.
